_note: Hand-reviewed prompt pack for the German definition and expression prompts.
Mined from the 2025 corpus (12,947 definition cells -- 4.2% fewer than the
other languages -- and 8,589 expression cells) by the same method as the
Chinese pack; the measured basis for every value is recorded in
One shipped cell substitutes a Greek beta for the German sharp s
(11036073:21056491, `äuβere` for `äußere`). That single cell is why the
script contract names both characters explicitly and why G-SCRIPT treats a
Greek letter inside a run of Latin letters as a BLOCK-tier defect.
COVERAGE METHOD for fixed_renderings_table: each percentage is the share of
definition cells whose DANISH definition contains the left-hand formula (for
the frame rows, the `der` form: `person der`, `noget der`) and whose target
gloss contains the right-hand rendering. Stated because a reviewer read the
`der/som` label as the denominator and could not land on the value: the
73.2% for person (EN/DE/ES), i.e. the whole table would shift, not one row.
Danish text in the worked examples is HAND-AUTHORED in DDO's editorial style.
No DDO source text is stored in this file.
allowed_scripts: Latin letters including ä, ö, ü and ß, German punctuation, and Arabic digits
orthography_rules: Write German with its own letters: ä, ö, ü and ß. NEVER substitute the Greek letter β for ß -- one shipped cell reads äuβere where äußere was meant, and it is invisible at a glance. Write compounds as one word, not hyphenated (0.49% of shipped lemmas contain a hyphen). Begin the `gloss` with a capital letter and end it with a single full stop (80.7% of cells; verb glosses are the least regular bucket at 67.4% against 98.8% for nouns).
lemma_charset_rule: German letters including ä, ö, ü and ß, plus spaces and rarely a hyphen. No article, no gender marker, no digits, no quotation marks.
punctuation_rule: German punctuation with ASCII marks. Commas are the norm (65.7% of glosses -- the house shape is a noun phrase followed by a relative clause) and a semicolon may carry a short synonym tail (15.2%). Colons (0.25%) and slashes (0.32%) are effectively absent; do not introduce them.
pos_vb: Give the bare lowercase infinitive: 95.9% of shipped verb-sense lemmas are lowercase and 85.9% end in -en, -ern or -eln. Keep `sich` when the verb is genuinely reflexive (7.1% of verb lemmas).
pos_sb: Capitalise the noun, but NEVER add der, die or das and never mark gender: only 0.33% of shipped noun lemmas carry an article, and those 18 cells are defects. Write a compound as one word.
pos_function: Open the `gloss` with `Wird` and name the use: 29.6% of function-word glosses and 80.1% of interjection glosses do this.

definitions.gloss: Der Vorgang, etwas mit Kraft zu sich hin zu bewegen.
Ein Strom kalter Luft, der sich durch einen Raum bewegt, z.B. von einer offenen Tür.
Eine charakteristische Eigenschaft einer Person oder Sache, oft eine, die leicht zu erkennen ist.

fixed_renderings_table: fx              -> z.B. (59.6%, and it beats `zum Beispiel` 3:1)
om person       -> auf eine Person bezogen
med hensyn til  -> in Bezug auf (74.1%)
anti_patterns: bad lemma das Haus -> an article in the lemma; only 0.33% of shipped noun lemmas carry der, die or das, and every one of them is a defect -> good lemma Haus
bad gloss Das äuβere Ende einer Stange. -> a Greek beta standing in for the German sharp s; exactly one cell shipped this way in 2025 -> good gloss Das äußere Ende einer Stange.
bad lemma Zug-Luft -> a hyphenated compound; only 0.49% of shipped lemmas contain a hyphen -> good lemma Zugluft

bad gloss Der Vorgang, etwas mit Kraft zu sich hin zu bewegen, was in der Physik Zugkraft heißt. -> over-explaining past the Danish definition (V4 gloss rule 2) -> good gloss Der Vorgang, etwas mit Kraft zu sich hin zu bewegen.
length_targets: lemma: one token is the norm (76.0% of cells), two 17.3%, three 5.6%. Median 10 characters, 90th percentile 17; the longest lemmas are solid compounds, which is correct.
gloss: 11 words is the median, 20 the 90th percentile, 32 the 99th; above 25 words needs a reason. Exactly one sentence, capital letter to a single full stop.
lemma_allowed_set: German letters including ä, ö, ü and ß, spaces, and hyphens
gloss_allowed_set: German letters including ä, ö, ü and ß, German punctuation including the low-9 and left double quotation marks, Arabic digits, the Danish letters æ ø å when a Danish word is named, and rarely a concise English word

fixed_expressions.gloss: Willensstark sein und sich durchsetzen können.
Völlig begeistert sein oder die Kontrolle vollständig verlieren.
